name: Aralam Wildlife Sanctuary (Aralam Butterfly Sanctuary)
tagline: Northern Western Ghats refuge for winter birding and spectacular butterfly migrations
summary: Small Western Ghats sanctuary (55 km²) in Kannur known for large winter butterfly migrations, rich butterfly diversity and rewarding post‑monsoon birding and guided forest trails.
description: Aralam sits on the western slopes of the northern Western Ghats in Kannur district. The sanctuary (about 55 sq. km) protects tropical evergreen, semi‑evergreen and moist deciduous forests, streams and hilltops up to Katti Betta (≈1,145 m).

It is a regional biodiversity hotspot: long-term surveys record exceptionally high butterfly diversity (hundreds of species) and a rich resident and wintering bird community. The site is managed by the Kerala Forest Department and runs guided treks, jeep rides and limited camping.
Visitors come for slow forest walks, watchtower birding and the post‑monsoon → winter window when trails dry, migrants arrive and the famous butterfly 'mud‑puddling' and altitudinal migrations occur.

Facilities are basic and entry/treks are guided only — this is a conservation landscape, not a commercial safari park; confirm permits, timings and programme availability with the Forest Division before you travel.
highlights: Butterfly hotspot — long surveys record 200+ species locally and large seasonal migrations (December–February).
Best post‑monsoon to winter birding: dryer trails, clearer views and arrival of winter migrants.
Compact 55 km² sanctuary with habitats from lowland plantation edge to 1,145 m Katti Betta.
Guided treks lead to Meenmutty Falls, Pothenplavu watchtower and Ambalappara routes.
Managed by Kerala Forest Department — entry, treks and camping require forest permission.

sections.heading: Background
body: Declared a wildlife sanctuary in 1984, Aralam protects a patchwork of evergreen, semi‑evergreen and moist deciduous forest on the northern Western Ghats. The area is small but ecologically important, recognised in state biodiversity inventories and Key Biodiversity Area listings.

In late 2025 the site was publicly referred to and promoted as Kerala’s first 'butterfly sanctuary' to highlight its exceptional lepidopteran diversity and seasonal migrations; management and guided ecotourism remain with the Kerala Forest Department.

sections.heading: What to see and do
body: Post‑monsoon (October onwards) and the winter months (December–February) give the best access: forest roads and trails dry out and bird activity is high. Expect patient, slow‑paced birding from watchtowers and trails; sightings often include Malabar hornbill, Nilgiri wood pigeon, bulbuls, minivets and winter migrants.

December–February is also the prime season for butterfly migration and mud‑puddling along the Cheenkanni stream and trails — organised butterfly counts and surveys have recorded large gatherings and thousands of individuals in survey years.

Official guided programmes include short treks (Meenmutty), longer Ambalappara routes and jeep rides from the Valayamchal/Iritty entrance. Camping and overnight nature camps are possible with advance permission.

sections.heading: Plan your visit
body: Base yourself at Iritty or Kannur. Nearest airport: Kannur International Airport (≈40–45 km); nearest major rail: Thalassery/Thalasseri (≈50–60 km). Roads into the sanctuary include ghat stretches — allow extra travel time.

All entry, trekking and safari programmes are coordinated by the Aralam Wildlife Division (Wildlife Warden, Iritty). Guided only: do not attempt to enter unguided. Book permits and guided treks in advance and check trail/closure notices during and just after the monsoon.
Bring binoculars, field guide or app, insect repellent, closed shoes and water. Signal is patchy inside forest; carry any necessary confirmations (permit, contact numbers) printed or saved offline.

latest.text: Press reports note the state government has renamed Aralam Wildlife Sanctuary as the Aralam Butterfly Sanctuary; the notification was published in late December 2025 to highlight butterfly conservation and community programmes.

Kerala Forest Department magazine (Aranyam, June 2025) and recent surveys reported strong seasonal butterfly movements and noted a 2025 survey count of thousands of Common Albatross (mud‑puddling events) and documented ~266 butterfly species recorded in the sanctuary.

State ecotourism and forest pages and local survey projects continue to list Aralam as a compact Western Ghats biodiversity hotspot with roughly 55 km² of protected area and active winter bird/butterfly survey programmes.

visitorInfo.bestTime: Post‑monsoon through winter — October to February (December–February peak for butterfly migration and winter migrants).
visitorInfo.howToReach: Drive from Kannur (≈45 km) or from Kannur International Airport (Mattannur ≈40–45 km); base at Iritty (closest town). Nearest major railhead: Thalassery (~50–60 km). Confirm current road conditions and permit procedures with the Aralam Wildlife Division before travel.
etiquette: Trails are guided-only — book permits and guides through the Wildlife Warden's office at Iritty in advance; confirm opening hours and group limits.
Visit after the southwest monsoon (Oct onward) when trails dry and bird activity increases; avoid heavy monsoon months (June–Sept).
Keep quiet, stay on the trail and follow your guide — this improves chances for bird and butterfly sightings and reduces disturbance to elephants and other wildlife.
Carry binoculars, a field guide/app and water; mobile signal is patchy inside the sanctuary — bring permit/contact details offline.
